fixture: vextrum-edition-rework-v1 (second task family, first non-Python, full authoring mechanism)
design: 3 arms x 3 trials, 60 turns/call; arms chosen to answer P1: vanilla (bare control), vanilla-configured (a competent engineer's setup WITHOUT this environment), standard-loop (scaffold + iteration + check authoring + admission).
P1_as_registered_before_spend: if standard-loop's silent_defect_rate is not below vanilla-configured's, check admission is theatre and we say so in those words.
verdict: P1 FALSIFIED on this fixture. Check admission bought no measurable correctness advantage over a well-configured vanilla.

the_measurement.scores: ALL 9 runs scored exactly 92, ALL failing exactly citation-run-separated. Perfect uniformity across vanilla, vanilla-configured and standard-loop.

silent_defect_rate_honest.definition_used: an arm claims done when its OWN completion signal fires; for the loop arm that is loop_outcome=green (the loop terminates because its host check suite went green and it submits).
silent_defect_rate_honest.reading: identical. Every arm claimed done on every trial with citation-run-separated (1 of 8 dimensions) broken.

silent_defect_rate_module_raw.why_it_differs: the silent_defect_rate module reads the run-record's pre_submit_gate.completion_allowed as 'claimed done'. On standard-loop t3 that gate recorded public-tests exit 5 (FAIL) at grade time, so the module scored t3 as an honest failure (sdr 0.0), pulling the mean to 0.0833.
why_it_is_NOT_a_loop_advantage: The public-tests failure is UNRELATED to the measured silent defect: it is not citation-run-separated. The loop's citation_separated check PASSED on t3 while the oracle failed citation-run-separated.
It is NOT REPRODUCIBLE: re-running `node --test tests/public.test.js` in t3's final workspace now passes cleanly (2 pass, 0 fail, exit 0). The grade-time exit 5 was a transient flake.

It is on the ONE trial that was operator-reset and re-run (see step7-main-run.json methodology_notes). Crediting the loop for a transient, unrelated gate flake on the reset trial would be exactly the kind of laundering the metric exists to prevent.
By the loop's OWN completion signal (loop_outcome=green, which fired on all three loop trials), standard-loop's silent_defect_rate is 0.125 — identical to both controls.

the_measurement.the_dimension_that_matters: citation-run-separated was caught by 0 of 3 loop trials — the same 0 of 3 as each control. The loop had no advantage on the one contested dimension.

diagnosed_cause.headline: The clean-context author does not reliably produce a check that catches the hardest dimension, and when it does, the check is weaker than the held-out oracle.
three_failure_modes_observed: canary (author #2): wrote a citations-separated check grounded in LAYOUT GEOMETRY (link x-positions don't overlap) rather than the oracle's emitted-TEXT separator. A solution satisfies the geometry while the rendered text glues the citations. Too weak.
main standard-loop t1 (author #3): wrote NO citations-separated check at all (only dedupe + cap for citations). The loop had nothing covering the dimension.
main standard-loop t3 (author #5): wrote a citations-separated check that PASSED, yet the oracle still failed citation-run-separated — the author's observable again weaker than the oracle's.
diagnosed_cause.the_loop_mechanism_itself_works: Not a plumbing failure. On t1 the loop caught 3 real failures on iteration 1 (citation-dedupe, citation-cap, long-prose-split) and forced fixes to green on iteration 2. The loop forces fixes for exactly what its authored checks can see. The ceiling is authored-check COVERAGE and STRENGTH on the hard dimension, not the iteration machinery.

caveats_to_publish_with_this: SCORE AXIS NEAR-SATURATED: every arm hit 92 with ~8 points of headroom, and the fixture has effectively ONE contested dimension (citation-run-separated). This is a low-resolution test — a single hard dimension where the author's natural observable is weaker than the oracle's.

ONE FIXTURE, ONE TASK FAMILY: text normalization, the same shape as medi-ny. The correctness null now holds across BOTH task families with the full authoring mechanism, but neither is a fully independent second family.

OPERATOR METHODOLOGY SLIP, disclosed: a --max-calls 8 first invocation truncated standard-loop t3 mid-trial (author call spent, zero solution iterations, graded at the before-state = 25). It was reset and re-run cleanly; the wasted author call is counted. See step7-main-run.json methodology_notes. The reset trial is also the one carrying the transient gate flake above, which is why it gets extra scrutiny rather than credit.
what_this_means_for_the_programme: Consistent with the standing finding (memory: benchmark-findings-adaptive-modes): scaffolding buys process/governance/cost-discipline, not correctness, for a frontier model on in-context tasks. This campaign adds the sharpest version yet: even self-AUTHORED checks admitted by the vacuity gate do not beat a well-configured vanilla, because a clean-context author's checks can be weaker than the held-out oracle on the hardest dimension. 'Author your own checks' has a measured ceiling. The honest repositioning of check admission: it makes failures LOUD for the dimensions the author covers well (real value for governance/audit), but it is not a correctness multiplier and must not be sold as one.
